_what: Standing director crossing rulings, read BY tools/batch_test/soak/wave_fence.py itself on every run (RULING 11, GH #729). A ruling that lives only in a report, a charter, or three flags the operator has to retype is a ruling whose default state is silence -- that is what cost W64.
_who_writes_this: The director, in the same work unit as the ruling. Nobody else. The batch desk READS it (by running the gate); it does not add rows.
_constraints: Every record goes through wave_fence.build_crossing(), so RULING 10's four constraints hold verbatim: the ceiling cannot reach the $90 brake or the owner's $100 approval line (refused, exit 2, never clamped); `expiry` is mandatory and checked at run time; `ref` is mandatory and printed verbatim; the gate announces the ruling on every run it touches, including the CLEAR one.
_expiry_semantics: An expired record here is NOT an error -- it is a record reaching its designed end of life. The gate keeps running, at the DERIVED fence, and says out loud that the ruling expired. (An expired ruling asserted via --director-crossing IS exit 2: there the operator claimed this round that it was live.) Retire expired records when convenient; leaving one costs a printed line, not a gate.
_two_live_at_once: Refused, exit 2. Which ceiling binds would otherwise be a bookkeeping accident. Superseding a ruling means removing the old row in the same edit.
